common.a: Yes. No sign-up, no subscription, no watermarks and no limit on the number of files.
No. Files are processed right in your browser and never leave your device — the site doesn't even have a server to upload them to.

common.q: Is there a file size limit?
common.a: There is no hard limit; it depends on your device's memory. Files of tens of megabytes work fine, while very large ones (150 MB and up) may run out of browser memory.

common.q: Does it work on a phone?
common.a: Yes, in any modern browser, with nothing to install. The editor is more comfortable on a computer, where a bigger screen makes precise placement easier.

steps: Open a PDF: drop the file on the page or click “Choose file”.
Pick a tool in the toolbar: text, image, shapes, highlighter, pen or whiteout.
Click “Download PDF” to save your changes to a new file.

faq.q: Can I change text that is already in the PDF?
faq.a: Yes, with the “Edit text” tool: click a line and type the new text. The old line is covered and the new one is written on top.

faq.q: What if I close the tab by accident?
faq.a: The editor keeps a draft in your browser and offers to continue where you left off next time. Drafts are not kept for password-protected files.

editText.howTo: How to change text in a PDF
steps: Open a PDF file.
Click the line you want to fix and type the new text.
Click “Download PDF”.

faq.q: Is the original text removed from the file?
faq.a: By default the old line is only covered and stays inside the file. To remove it completely, turn on “Rasterize pages with text edits” when downloading — those pages become images.

faq.q: Why can't I select text in a scan?
faq.a: In a scan, text is part of an image. Cover it with the “Whiteout” tool and type new text on top.

steps: Open a PDF — the signature window appears right away.
Draw your signature with a mouse or finger, type your name in a handwriting font, or upload a photo of your signature.
Drag the signature into place, resize it if needed and download the file.

faq.q: Is this a legally binding electronic signature?
faq.a: No, it's an image of your signature — like signing a printout and scanning it. The site does not create certificate-based digital signatures.

faq.q: Can I save my signature for next time?
faq.a: Yes, check “Remember this signature on this device”. It is stored only in your browser.

forms.howTo: How to fill in a PDF form
steps: Open a PDF with fillable fields.
Click a field and type, tick checkboxes, pick options from lists.
Click “Download PDF”.

faq.q: What if the file has no fields?
faq.a: Then the form is just text with lines. Pick the “Text” tool and type right on the lines.

faq.q: Can I stop the fields from being changed later?
faq.a: Yes: in the download options, turn on “Make form fields read-only” — the values become part of the page.

steps: Choose or drop several PDF files.
Put them in order by dragging, or click “By name”.
Click “Merge” to download a single file.

faq.q: How many files can I merge?
faq.a: As many as you like — the only limit is your device's memory.

faq.q: Can I merge only some of the pages?
faq.a: Yes, with the “Pages” tool: add several PDFs, delete the pages you don't need and arrange the rest.

steps: Choose a PDF file.
Enter page ranges (e.g. 1-3, 5, 8-), split every N pages, or into single pages.
Click “Split”. Several files are downloaded as one ZIP archive.

faq.q: How do I extract several pages into one file?
faq.a: Enter them as ranges and turn on “Save all selected pages as a single file”.

faq.q: Does quality get worse?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied as they are, without recompression.

organize.howTo: How to rotate, delete or reorder pages
steps: Open a PDF to see thumbnails of all pages.
Drag pages around, rotate or delete them, add blank pages or pages from other PDFs.
Click “Save PDF”.

faq.q: Can I select several pages at once?
faq.a: Yes: Shift- or Ctrl-click, or use “Select all”. Rotation and deletion apply to every selected page.

faq.q: Does page quality change?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied without recompression, and rotation doesn't affect quality.

imagesToPdf.howTo: How to make a PDF from images
steps: Choose images: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or BMP.
Put them in order and pick the page size, orientation and margins.
Click “Create PDF”.

faq.q: How do I turn phone photos of a document into a PDF?
faq.a: Take photos of the pages, open this site on your phone and select the photos — you'll get a single PDF.

faq.q: Do images lose quality?
faq.a: JPG and PNG are embedded as they are, without recompression. WebP, GIF, BMP and rotated JPGs are re-encoded at high quality.

pdfToImages.howTo: How to save a PDF as JPG or PNG
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick the format, quality and pages.
Click “Convert”. Several pages are downloaded as a ZIP archive.

faq.q: Which quality should I choose?
faq.a: 72 DPI is for viewing on screen, 150 is a good all-rounder, 300 is for printing. Higher DPI means larger files.

faq.q: PNG or JPG?
faq.a: PNG is lossless and better for text and diagrams. JPG is much smaller — good for photos and scans.

ocr.howTo: How to recognize text in a PDF
steps: Choose a scanned PDF.
Select the text languages: Russian, English, Ukrainian, German, French or Spanish.
Click “Recognize” and download a searchable PDF or a plain .txt.

faq.q: What changes in the PDF after recognition?
faq.a: Nothing visible: invisible text is added on top of the pages, so search and copying start working.

faq.q: Why does the first run take longer?
faq.a: Your browser downloads the recognition models from this site once (about 10 MB for English and Russian) and caches them.

steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick the compression level: light, recommended or maximum.
Click “Compress” — you'll see how much smaller the file got and can download it.

faq.q: Why did the file barely shrink?
faq.a: Compression mostly works on images inside the PDF. A text-only file is already compact and can't be made smaller without losses.

faq.q: What does maximum compression do?
faq.a: Pages are turned into lower-resolution images. The file gets much smaller, but text can no longer be selected or searched.

steps: Choose a PDF file.
Enter a password twice. Optionally restrict printing, copying and editing.
Click “Protect PDF” and download the file.

faq.q: How strong is the protection?
faq.a: It uses AES-256 encryption, the same standard as Adobe Acrobat. The strength depends on the password itself, so choose a long, non-obvious one.

faq.q: What if I forget the password?
faq.a: The file can't be opened — the password isn't stored anywhere and can't be recovered. Keep it somewhere safe.

unlock.howTo: How to remove a password from a PDF
steps: Choose a protected PDF.
Enter the password when asked.
Click “Remove protection” to download a copy without the password.

faq.q: Can I remove a password I don't know?
faq.a: No, the site doesn't crack passwords. But if a file only restricts printing or copying and has no password to open it, those restrictions are removed without a password.

faq.q: Does anything change in the document itself?
faq.a: No, the content stays the same — only the encryption is removed.
